newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Sampoerna says in alliance talk with Salim.
newsitem.headline: Sampoerna says in alliance talk with Salim.

text.p: Indonesian blue chip cigarette maker PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna said on Friday it was considering forming an alliance with Indonesia's largest conglomerate the Salim Group to boost the company's performance.

"We are having talks with the Salim Group. The areas where we can cooperate include retailing and printing. But the talks are still at their initial stage," president director Putra Sampoerna told a news conference following the firm's annual shareholders' meeting.
Shareholders approved the company's proposal to pay a dividend of 150 rupiah per share for 1996.
Putra Sampoerna said the cooperation was likely to include helping each other in distribution and retailing of the consumer products of both parties.

The Salim Group, headed by Indonesian Chinese Liem Sioe Liong, is a widely-diversified business group with interests in banking, property, food, cement, chemicals, automotives, broadcasting, trading and agribusiness.
Putra Sampoerna, however, denied recent rumours of a possible share swap in the near term between the two parties.
